title: Coherent endpoint normalization of a cartesian twisted comma
statement:
Use quasicategories, ordinary nerves, coherent functors and transformations, functor simplicial sets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], ordered joins of [lem-cbc-relative-coslice-left-fibration], and cartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Work in one containing universe. Let $A$ be an ordinary category. Let $K=N(T)$, where $T$ has objects $u:a\to b$ in $A$ and arrows $(f,g):u\to u'$ with $f:a\to a'$, $g:b'\to b$, $u=gu'f$. Let $\pi:K\to N(A)^{\mathrm{op}}$ send $u:a\to b$ to $b$. Let $p:R\to N(A)^{\mathrm{op}}$ be cartesian and let $k:K\to R$ satisfy $pk=\pi$. Assume $k$ sends every arrow $(1_a,g):gu'\to u'$ to a $p$-cartesian edge. No terminal-object assumption is made.

For $r\in R_c$, define $R_{r/}$ by $(R_{r/})_m=\{\Delta^0\star\Delta^m\to R\text{ with first vertex }r\}$, projecting to its remaining face, and put $C_r=K\times_R R_{r/}$. An object of $C_r$ is $(u:a\to b,\beta:r\to k(u))$; its projected edge uniquely has the form $w^{\mathrm{op}}:c\to b$ for $w:b\to c$. There are a functor $H:C_r\to C_r$ and a transformation $\eta:H\to\mathrm{id}_{C_r}$ with the following descriptions. $H$ sends this object to $(wu:a\to c,h:r\to k(wu))$, with $p(h)=1_c$. The component of $\eta$ has twisted pair $(1_a,w):wu\to u$ and a triangle $\beta\simeq k(1_a,w)h$. On a comma arrow whose twisted pair is $(f,g)$, the base triangle gives $w'=wg$, and the underlying twisted pair of its image under $H$ is $(f,1_c):wu\to w'u'$. These objectwise factorizations and triangles can be chosen on all simplices so as to define $H$ and $\eta$ coherently, including all faces and degeneracies. For each specified $\beta$, the space of its factorizations together with the triangle is contractible. The entire construction allows $R$ to be larger than the universe in which $A$ is small.

source.place: Agent coherent endpoint-normalization lemma extracted from returned step 2; cartesian factorization of the full join comma, not only its homotopy category.

proof.text: Put $B=N(A)^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $C=C_r$, and let $j:C\to K$ be projection. The universal comma simplex gives a map $b:\Delta^0\star C\to R$ with apex $r$ and boundary $kj$: on each simplex of $C$ this is precisely its defining join map, so the maps agree under every operator. The coslice projection $R_{r/}\to R$ is a left fibration by the relative-coslice theorem, taking its index $\Delta^0$ and empty subindex. Its pullback $C\to K$ is a left fibration: a horn lifting square is just the corresponding square over $R$ with its fixed $K$-simplex. Nerves of ordinary categories fill inner horns by composing their successive arrows (associativity checks the faces), so $K$, and hence $C$, are quasicategories.

source.place: Agent expansion of the endpoint-normalization subargument in the twisted comma resolution serving proof paragraph 2.

proof.text: Define an ordinary category $D$ with objects $(u:a\to b,w:b\to c)$, and arrows $(f,g):(u,w)\to(u',w')$ satisfying $u=gu'f$ and $w'=wg$. Its identities are $(1,1)$; the composite of $(f,g)$ and $(f',g')$ is $(f'f,gg')$, and $w''=w' g'=wgg'$. Thus all relations are preserved by composition. Applying $p$ to each defining simplex of $C$ gives a simplex of the ordinary coslice $c/B$ together with its $K$-simplex. Reading its arrows gives a simplicial map $t:C\to N(D)$. This is exact in every degree: a simplex of an ordinary nerve is its string of arrows, so the base triangle for each comma edge imposes $w'=wg$, and its longer faces impose exactly the composite relations just written.

source.place: Agent expansion of the endpoint-normalization subargument in the twisted comma resolution serving proof paragraph 2.

proof.text: There are functors $J,N:D\to T$ with $J(u,w)=u$, $J(f,g)=(f,g)$ and $N(u,w)=wu$, $N(f,g)=(f,1_c)$. Indeed $wu=wgu'f=w'u'f$, so the last pair is an arrow of $T$; identities and composites follow from their displayed formulas. The arrows $e_{(u,w)}=(1_a,w):wu\to u$ define a natural transformation $e:N\to J$: along $(f,g)$ its two composites are $(f,wg)$ and $(f,w')$, equal by $w'=wg$. Taking nerves and precomposing $t$ gives $E:C\times\Delta^1\to K$ from $n=Nt$ to $j=Jt$. Applying $k$ gives $q=kE$. Every vertical edge of $q$ is Cartesian by the hypothesis on $k$.

source.place: Agent expansion of the endpoint-normalization subargument in the twisted comma resolution serving proof paragraph 2.

proof.text: Give $C\times\Delta^1$ the marking consisting of degenerate edges and every vertical edge $\{v\}\times\Delta^1$, and give $C\times\{1\}$ its induced marking. The selectively marked terminal-cylinder theorem, with $K=C$, $K'=\varnothing$ and its vertex set $A=C_0$, says that $i:C\times\{1\}\hookrightarrow C\times\Delta^1$ is marked anodyne: every nondegenerate simplex of $C$ has final vertex in $C_0$. Thus $q$ takes every marked edge to a Cartesian edge; its degenerate images are Cartesian by the degenerate-edge assertion of the cocartesian composition theorem applied to $p^{\mathrm{op}}$ (reversing horns interchanges the two predicates).

source.place: Lemma 3.2.1.9, printed p.173, specialized to empty subcomplex and all vertices.

proof.text: Construct a base cone $v:\Delta^0\star(C\times\Delta^1)\to B$ with apex $c$ as follows. On $D\times[1]$, the base of $kE$ is constant $c$ at time $0$ and sends $(u:a\to b,w)$ to $b$ at time $1$. The cone leg at time $0$ is $1_c$; at time $1$ it is $w^{\mathrm{op}}:c\to b$. The relation $w'=wg$ proves naturality on time-$1$ arrows, and the vertical arrows are precisely $w^{\mathrm{op}}$; all mixed squares commute by the same equality. This defines an ordinary functor on the category obtained by adjoining an initial vertex to $D\times[1]$. Its nerve, precomposed with $\Delta^0\star(t\times\operatorname{id})$, is $v$. In particular $v|_{C\times\Delta^1}=pq$ and $v|_{\Delta^0\star(C\times\{1\})}=pb$, since these maps to an ordinary nerve have the same edge strings.

source.place: Agent expansion of the endpoint-normalization subargument in the twisted comma resolution serving proof paragraph 2.

proof.text: Apply the Cartesian marked-slice restriction theorem to $p:R\to B$, the marked inclusion $i$ in step 4, and $q=kE$. The cone pair $(b,v)$ is a vertex of its target $R_{/q|_1}\times_{B_{/pq|_1}}B_{/pq}$. Surjectivity on vertices of this trivial Kan fibration gives a cone $\Phi:\Delta^0\star(C\times\Delta^1)\to R$, extending $q$, restricting exactly to $b$ at time $1$, and with $p\Phi=v$. The restriction to $b$ fixes the apex to be exactly $r$, even when $C$ is empty. This is one lift of the full cone; it chooses all simplex data together, rather than attempting independent vertex choices.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.11, printed p.151, applied to the marked terminal cylinder.

proof.text: A map $\Delta^0\star X\to R$ with fixed apex $r$ is the same as a simplicial map $X\to R_{r/}$: restrict to $\Delta^0\star\Delta^m$ for each simplex of $X$, and conversely glue these restrictions. Applying this to $\Phi$ gives $\lambda:C\times\Delta^1\to R_{r/}$ with remaining face $q=kE$. Hence $(E,\lambda)$ defines a simplicial map $\widetilde\eta:C\times\Delta^1\to K\times_RR_{r/}=C$. Its time-$1$ restriction is exactly the identity, because $E|_1=j$ and $\Phi|_1=b$. Put $H=\widetilde\eta|_0$ and let $\eta$ be this transformation. At $(u,w,\beta)$ the time-$0$ edge is $h:r\to k(wu)$ over $1_c$, while its vertical triangle is $\beta\simeq k(1_a,w)h$. On a comma arrow $(f,g)$ the time-$0$ pair is $(f,1_c)$, as required. Faces and degeneracies commute because $\Phi$ and $E$ are simplicial maps, so this proves the full coherent assertion.

source.place: Agent expansion of the endpoint-normalization subargument in the twisted comma resolution serving proof paragraph 2.

proof.text: For a specified $\beta:r\to k(u)$ over $w^{\mathrm{op}}$, repeat the slice-restriction theorem with $i:\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$, the final edge marked, and $q=k(1_a,w):k(wu)\to k(u)$. This $i$ is marked anodyne by the cylinder theorem with $K=\Delta^0$. Take the fiber over the cone $\beta$ and the base triangle with legs $1_c,w^{\mathrm{op}}$. Its vertices are exactly pairs $(h,\beta\simeq qh)$, and its higher simplices are maps $\Delta^m\star\Delta^1\to R$ with their initial $\Delta^m$ fixed at $r$ and the prescribed restrictions. This fiber $F\to\Delta^0$ is a trivial Kan fibration: each boundary lifting problem is the same problem for the original restriction map, over its constant target vertex. By the trivial-Kan lifting theorem it fills every horn, hence $F$ is Kan. The trivial-Kan homotopy-equivalence theorem makes $F\to\Delta^0$ a simplicial homotopy equivalence, and the simplicial-homotopy-to-weak-equivalence theorem gives weak contractibility. Finally take all constructions in a universe containing $R$ and $A$; neither the cylinder nor slice theorem bounds their size in the smaller universe of $A$. No terminal objects or terminal-object preservation have been used.
